title: Chapter 284: Jiang Ling
html:
The little girl stopped crying and turned to stare blankly at Chen Ge. Tears covered her palm-sized face, and a watery haze veiled her reddened eyes. Her pitiful expression could have softened the cruelest heart. Unable to resist, the nurse scooped her up, pressed her cheek against the child’s head, and gently patted her back.

Had the scene contained only the nurse and the two children, it would have been heartwarming: an older sister doing everything she could to care for her younger siblings, finding happiness in family despite hardship. Chen Ge’s presence, however, transformed the tableau into something uncanny.

He stood rigid in the doorway, like a traveler stranded in the wilderness while a predator watched from the dark.Judging by the proportions in Fan Yu’s drawing, the monster is roughly three times the size of an adult.

Chen Ge already knew that Fan Yu could see ghosts. In other words, the spiderlike creature in the drawing was truly standing behind him.

His finger hovered over the recorder as veins stood out along his arm. He had never expected to encounter a monster in such a warm, welcoming children’s home.

“Fan Yu seems close to the girl, and he knows me. Wouldn’t that make me her friend too?” Chen Ge murmured from the doorway, keeping his voice low but loud enough for anything behind him to hear.

“Don’t cry. Big Sister has gone for now. We’ll find her tomorrow.” Fan Yu ruffled the girl’s hair, showing her unusual gentleness.

“Okay.” The girl rubbed her swollen eyes, slipped from the nurse’s arms, and reluctantly sat on a small chair. She continued clutching the dead spider, refusing to discard it.

When Fan Yu said the girl’s sister had left, Chen Ge released a quiet breath. He entered the room, picked up a broom, and began sweeping the glass into a corner.

Left standing in the middle of the room, the nurse felt awkwardly ignored.

“Mr. Chen, let me handle that.” She swept the shards into a dustpan, then smoothly ushered him from the room.

“You’ve seen the situation yourself.” Helplessness filled the nurse’s voice. “I’ve cared for Jiang Ling since she arrived nearly six months ago. She used to call me Mother and never leave my side. She was like a little angel. But after Fan Yu arrived, everything changed. Now she follows him everywhere and listens to no one else.”

“Why do I hear envy in your complaint?” Chen Ge leaned against the wall. He had a good impression of this Children’s Home; they were doing good work.

“I’m not jealous!” The nurse glared at him. “I’d never stop Jiang Ling from playing with other children, but Fan Yu is different. You’ve seen what he draws. Do you think a six-year-old girl should look at those pictures every day?”

“They certainly aren’t age-appropriate.” Chen Ge had no idea how to explain the truth to her.

“It’s much worse than inappropriate!” The nurse closed the door and pulled Chen Ge into a corner of the living room. “Jiang Ling was found at a murder scene. You have no idea what she endured. When she arrived six months ago, she wouldn’t speak and was terrified of everyone. Doctor Chen spent half a year counseling her, and she had finally begun to improve.”

Chen Ge’s expression turned serious. “Do you mind telling me about Jiang Ling’s past?”

The nurse lowered her voice. “I only know what the police told us. Jiang Ling came from a happy family of four who lived outside the city. They weren’t wealthy, but they were content. Her father was an honest farmer. Her mother, who didn’t appear local, was fair and beautiful. Jiang Ling’s older sister had inherited her mother’s looks.

“About a year ago, her father took out a loan to buy land for a peach orchard. Their home stood well beyond an already isolated village, far from other people. Just as the peaches ripened and their prospects began to improve, disaster struck.”

The nurse sighed, anger and sorrow entering her voice. “First Jiang Ling’s sister disappeared. Not long afterward, both parents died. Someone had mixed a large amount of rat poison into their food; the killer unquestionably intended to murder them.”

“Has the killer been caught?”

“No.” The nurse shook her head. “The police revealed very little. I only know that no money was stolen and it wasn’t a crime of passion. I suspect a villager did it out of envy. The farm was so isolated that no outsider would have gone there. And several days before the poisoning, Jiang Ling’s father caught a villager stealing ripening peaches. They fought in the orchard.”

After hearing her account, Chen Ge also considered the villagers plausible suspects. Murder usually required a motive, and revenge was a powerful one.

“The investigation failed to identify a suspect in the village. Jiang Ling, who hadn’t eaten the poisoned soup, was the only survivor. Perhaps seeing her parents collapse left her catatonic. The police believed she might have seen the killer, but they couldn’t communicate with her. After that night, her mental state was never the same.

“As you saw, she calls every spider her big sister. Most people recoil from such creatures, but she seeks them out. Can you imagine a little girl leaning close to webs and whispering affectionately to the spiders?

“As I got to know her, I noticed other problems. Her understanding of family is distorted. She calls the quilt on her bed Mother and a rope hanging from the ceiling Father. We’ve asked her why, but she can’t explain.”

The nurse’s sorrow made her affection for Jiang Ling obvious. “We’ve worked hard to correct those associations, and she has finally stopped calling the quilt and rope her parents. Once she stops treating spiders as her sister, she may be able to lead a normal life. But within days of arriving, Fan Yu undid nearly all our progress.”

“Let’s set Fan Yu aside for now.” Chen Ge needed ghosts to confront the Ghost Stories Society, so Jiang Ling’s sister interested him far more. “Did the police investigate the sister? Why did she disappear? Could she have been the killer?”

“The police did suspect that the killer could be Jiang Ling’s sister, but even now, they have not found Jiang Ling’s sister.”
